newsitem.title: HUNGARY: EDF to sell stakes in Hungarian power companies.
newsitem.headline: EDF to sell stakes in Hungarian power companies.

text.p: Electricite de France said on Friday it planned to sell some of its shares in two regional electricity companies in Hungary but would remain the strategic leader in the two firms.
"We will only sell enough shares for EDF to remain the industrial leader," Pierre Abou, EDF's representative in Hungary, told Reuters.

EDF acquired a 47.55 percent stake in southern regional power distributor EDASZ and 47.98 in south-eastern supplier DEMASZ in December last year when Hungary sold minority stakes in six electricity distributors and two power plants to investors from France, Germany and Belgium.

The sales contracts do not allow EDF to sell its shares in EDASZ and DEMASZ without the agreement of the state privatisation agency APV, whom Abou said would only allow EDF to offload shares to a strategic investor.

The Hungarian economic daily Vilaggazdassag on Friday reported that up to half the French company's EDASZ package could go to German firm Bayernwerke AG while an up-to-30 percent stake in DEMASZ was expected to be sold to Austrian EVN.
Abou was unable to reveal the size of the stakes for sale but confirmed EDF was talking to the Austrian and German companies.
"Bayernwerke and EVN have been quoted for a long time and are still interested in this operation," he said.

Bayernwerk AG currently holds a 47.25 percent in another Hungarian electricity distributor DEDASZ. Under privatisation rules, each investor is allowed to hold stakes in no more than two supply companies.
Abou said the sale was not connected to the Hungarian government's decision last week to postpone energy price rises to January 1 from October 1, a move which surprised investors at the time.
"We intended to sell the shares nearly from the beginning," he said. "It is part of the (company's) global doctrine."

Abou confirmed that representatives of all the Western utilities with investments in Hungary met privatisation minister Tamas Suchman to discuss the delayed rises but he said he was unable to disclose the result of the meeting.
